BiblicalUsage: Keiro means to shear, to cut the hair or the fleece. Acts 8:32 quotes the scripture, he was led as a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb dumb before his shearer, so opened he not his mouth. Acts 18:18 says Paul, having shorn his head in Cenchrea, for he had a vow. 1 Corinthians 11:6 says if the woman be not covered, let her also be shorn.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the shearer is the picture of the whole gospel: the Lamb dumb before his shearer opened not his mouth, and so we were saved. I hold that Paul's shorn head and the church's covering both say the same thing, that a vow is kept in the open.
